title: Add revenue and labels to order lines
prompt: Add three columns to `items`: `revenue` (quantity × unit price × (1 − discount)), `discount_band` (`"none"` when the discount is 0, `"small"` when it is above 0 and at most 0.10, `"big"` when it is above 0.10), and `is_bulk` (a boolean, `True` when quantity is 4 or more). Then set `total_revenue` to the sum of `revenue`, rounded to 2 decimals. Keep all 3,991 rows.
hints: Assigning to a new column name, `items["revenue"] = ...`, creates the column for every row.
For the bands, set `items["discount_band"] = "none"` first, then overwrite with `items.loc[mask, "discount_band"] = "small"` and again for `"big"`, broadest condition first.
A comparison already returns booleans: `items["is_bulk"] = items["quantity"] >= 4`.
explanation: Column arithmetic computes every line's revenue at once, and the total, 471,940.08, matches the lesson. The bands follow the default-then-overwrite pattern: every row starts as `none`, discounted rows become `small`, and rows above 10% are overwritten to `big`, giving 3,367 / 231 / 393. `np.select` with a list of conditions would also work. `is_bulk` needs no `np.where` at all: a comparison is already a boolean column. Every change was a direct assignment to `items`, which is the Copy-on-Write-safe way to modify a DataFrame.

checks.bands: `discount_band` splits lines into none 3,367 / small 231 / big 393
checks.bulk: `is_bulk` is a boolean column with 126 bulk lines
